Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNoHeaderMap()` uses `CSVParser.parse` with `CSVFormat.DEFAULT`, which means no explicit header is defined in the format. The test expects that calling `parser.getHeaderMap()` returns `null` if there is no header configured.

Looking at the source code, `CSVParser` has a field `headerMap` which is initialized in the constructor by calling `initializeHeader()`. The `initializeHeader()` method returns a `Map<String,Integer>` only if the format header is non-null; otherwise, it returns `null`.

In `getHeaderMap()`, however, it unconditionally constructs a new `LinkedHashMap` from `this.headerMap` and returns it. If `this.headerMap` is `null`, this call results in a `NullPointerException` because the `LinkedHashMap` constructor does not accept null.

Hence, the root cause is that `getHeaderMap()` does not check if `headerMap` is `null` before attempting to construct a new `LinkedHashMap`. Instead, it should either return `null` directly or handle the `null` case gracefully.

The bug report matches this reasoning: invoking `getHeaderMap()` when there is no header configured throws an NPE. The test expects `null`, but the current implementation triggers the NPE due to `new LinkedHashMap<>(null)`.

No relevant recent bug reports were found, so this diagnosis relies on the current code and test evidence.

This explains the failure and the NullPointerException seen in the bug report.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNoHeaderMap()` creates a CSVParser with a CSVFormat that has no header defined (CSVFormat.DEFAULT). According to the test, calling `parser.getHeaderMap()` should return `null` if there is no header.

However, the current implementation of `CSVParser.getHeaderMap()` always creates a new LinkedHashMap from `this.headerMap`. If `this.headerMap` is `null` (which it will be when there is no header configured), this leads to a NullPointerException when invoking `new LinkedHashMap<>(null)`.

Looking at the constructor and `initializeHeader()`, when no header is specified, the `headerMap` field is initialized to `null`. The `initializeHeader()` function only creates a LinkedHashMap if the header is non-null; otherwise, it returns `null`.

Therefore, the bug is that `getHeaderMap()` does not check whether `headerMap` is null before attempting to create a new LinkedHashMap instance from it. The correct behavior would be to return `null` immediately if `headerMap` is `null`.

This explains the NPE observed and the failed test where `assertNull(parser.getHeaderMap())` was expected but an exception was thrown instead.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
